messages:
Alex: Heads up — p95 on paged-flashattn jumped after kernel-selector change (commit c3f9a). Baseline ~120ms -> now ~210ms for seq=1024 under our concurrency=64 perf job. Noticed in tonight's smoke.
Priya: :eyes: same workload and batch sizes as baseline?
Alex: Same workload, same 64 concurrency and token distro. The selector switched to aggressive_grouping at runtime. I ran single-node benchmark.
Mike: Could be KV coldstart noise — did kv cache hit rate change? Also which Flash variant got chosen (flash_v1 vs fused_flash)?
Alex: Selector picked fused_flash for seq=1024; fallback to flash_v1 for lower seqs. KV hit rate stayed ~98% in logs. Quick perf profile I captured: 
```
hotspots:
  attention_kernel_fused: 42%
  kernel_dispatch_overhead: 22%
  memcpy: 18%
  thread_spin: 6%
```
Priya: That dispatch overhead jump looks suspicious. Any recent change in kernel launch path or per-batch bookkeeping?
Jordan: I merged a small change to selector heuristics to be batch-aware — could be adding copies. Reverting locally drops p95 to ~125ms for same job.
Alex: Can you paste the revert diff? We should bisect the commit range and validate. Running with selector=legacy yields p95 118ms.
bench-bot: nightly/seq1024/concurrency64: p95=210ms (commit c3f9a) — compare nightly/prev: p95=119ms
Mike: Plan: bisect between c3f1x -> c3f9a. Priya, can you run a microbench isolating kernel dispatch (no KV/caching, single batch) with perf counters?
Priya: On it. I'll also try disabling memcpy optimization to confirm where time goes.
Alex: Short-term mitigation: bias selector to prefer flash_v1 for seq>=512 until we fix. That avoids fused path.
Jordan: I'll open a revert PR and add extra tracing in kernel-selector to log decision/latency.
Priya: Microbench results: dispatch overhead went 18ms -> 52ms after selector change. memcpy is unchanged. Looks like selector added a per-batch memcpy for alignment when fused_flash selected.
Alex: Nice find. So the alignment copy is the culprit for the tail. We should avoid extra copy for already-aligned tensors. Jordan, want me to draft a fix?
Jordan: Please. If a fast patch isn't ready we'll land the revert and ship canary.
Alex: Drafted PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4521 — includes fix, unit tests, and microbench. Canaries scheduled on dedicated pool.
Priya: Local apply -> p95 returns to 122ms. Running canary now on a 10-node slice.
Mike: Thanks. If canary shows regression we'll flip runtime flag to fallback to flash_v1. Keep channel posted.
Alex: Will post canary metrics once probation completes. :thumbsup:
